What it is
Part 1 · Meet PBgif
Chapter 1 of 18

Send the perfect GIF with your photos as a PBgif.

You're not stuck with the same old GIFs anymore. Now you can make them with your friends and your own photos, in seconds. Pick the moment, type a caption, send it. A few taps and it's done. So easy even your grandma can do it.

Next Why it exists ↓
Why it exists
Chapter 2 of 18

Reaction GIFs with your friends in them.

You're always sending GIFs as a reaction. But wouldn't it be way better if those same GIFs had your friends in them, or said exactly what you wanted to say? That's PBgif: the classic GIF, made and customized exactly how you want it.

Make a PBgif
Chapter 6 of 18

Make a PBgif. A few taps.

Tap Make a PBgif. Shoot a Live Photo or a short video, or pick one you have. Pick the part you want, type the top and bottom text, tap Make it, then send. It's right in Messages too, with your PBgifs first.

Every PBgif you make is kept in My PBgifs. Play it again, edit it later, or save it to Photos.

Free and paid
Chapter 8 of 18

Free to make. Paid to go big.

PBgif is free: every ready-made recipe, PBgifs up to 3 seconds, the little slice badge in the corner, and small ads (never on your PBgif).

Go paid and you get:

  • No badge, no ads. Just your PBgif.
  • Twice as long. PBgifs up to 6 seconds.
  • Slow-mo and fast. Speed it up or slow it down.
  • Pick my own zoom. Choose who the recipe zooms in on.
  • The Kitchen. Customize any recipe and make it yours.
  • Your GIFs too. Turn the GIFs already on your phone into PBgifs.

On the way: seasonal recipes, and custom ones for your big days.

Next The name ↓
The name
Part 3 · The brand
Chapter 9 of 18

Why PBgif? PB and J. And jif.

Everybody knows how to make a PB&J. It's the go-to lunch: fast, easy, and hard to mess up. That's exactly how making a PBgif should feel.

And the gif part? People still argue about how to say GIF. Steve Wilhite, the guy who invented the GIF in 1987, said it's “jif,” like the peanut butter. He even joked, “Choosy developers choose GIF.” So PBgif says it his way: PB‑jif. PB and J, all in one.

That's the whole look too: cream bread, grape jelly, a picnic cloth, and sandwich puns in the little words.

Next The logo ↓
The logo
Chapter 10 of 18

The letters are the spread.

PB in peanut butter, gif in grape jelly, squished onto a slice of bread with a toasted rim.

Slide between glossy and flat. Glossy everywhere it can go, shirts too. Flat for screen print.

How small can it go?

Which logo when

Five versions. Pick the one that fits the spot.

1 · MainThe glossy slice.UseThe app icon, the intro, the App Store, big on plain backgrounds.Don'tTiny sizes, busy photos, or printing in one color.
2 · Flat sliceSame slice, no shine.UseSmall sizes, printing, stickers, and the badge on PBgifs.Don'tBig, where the glossy one fits.
3 · Outline sliceThe crust outline and the letters, no bread inside.UseOn plain light backgrounds (Bread or White), where a filled slice feels too heavy.Don'tLavender, Grape Jelly, dark colors or photos (use the one-color logo there), or tiny.
4 · Letters onlyJust the PB and gif letters, flat.UseWide or tight spots like headers and shirts, or when the slice is already showing nearby.Don'tThe app icon, the PBgif badge, or where people don't know PBgif yet.
5 · One colorAll one brand color: Burnt Toast, or white on photos and dark.UseWhenever the full-color logo is hard to read against what's behind it: Burnt Toast on light, white on photos and dark. Also one-color printing, embroidery, stamps, see‑through watermarks.Don'tWhen full color is possible.

Every version: never stretch it, only brand colors, no added effects, and always leave space around it.

The colors
Chapter 12 of 18

Grape Jelly on fresh Bread.

Reading text is Burnt Toast. In the app, Grape Jelly is only for things you can tap. The tour and guide also use it for headlines and labels. Every color pair is checked so the words are easy to read.

1 · Brand colors

Strict. Every button, word, screen and the cloth.

The color of the main button on every screen, like Make a PBgif and Send it. Also the plates, the chosen pill, switches when they're on, and links. If it's the main thing to tap, it's Grape Jelly.
What a Grape Jelly button turns while your finger is on it. Also the words on light lavender, like the pill choices that aren't picked.
The darker checks of the gingham cloth on the app icon and in the intro. Grape Jelly words are still easy to read on it.
The light purple strip behind pill choices like Recent / Most used. The chosen pill is shiny Grape Jelly and slides along it. It's also the off side of switches, little labels and soft boxes.
The second choice next to a Grape Jelly button, like Make another or Maybe later. Peanut butter and jelly, always together.
The color behind everything in the app, like a slice of bread. Every panel you swipe down is this cream all the way to the edges.
Titles and everything you read. Also the Delete button, the only button with a bite out of it.
Small helper words: notes under things, "Sent 3 times", hints. Softer than reading text, still easy to read.
The light squares of the gingham cloth, and the cards that hold things on the tour and guide pages.

Tap a color to copy its code. RGB is for screens, CMYK is for print, and Pantone is the closest ink.

2 · Logo colors

Only in the logo, the PB titles and button shading. Never for text.

The PB letters in the logo.
The golden crust around the bread slice.
The soft inside of the slice, behind the letters.
The dark toasted outline around the slice. It's always there.
The gif letters in the logo. The same color as the brand Grape Jelly.
Darker jelly that shades the gif letters, and the shadowy bottom of Grape Jelly buttons.
The shiny highlights on the jelly letters.
The soft, puffy glow inside the PB titles.

3 · Helper colors

Rare, for special jobs.

The “Don't” labels and warnings. Used rarely, never for buttons.

4 · Free colors

Anything goes inside the content: your photos, your PBgifs, seasonal and holiday recipes, recipe ads. A Halloween pack can be orange and black inside its card, but the buttons, words and screens around it stay brand colors. Words still have to be easy to read.

Round, friendly, and very meme.

Fredoka for titles and the main button. SF Pro Rounded for the rest of the app, at Apple's sizes (Apple only lets it be used on Apple devices, so outside the app Nunito stands in). Anton only for the meme captions on PBgifs, nowhere else.

The titles
Chapter 14 of 18

Written in peanut butter.

Every chapter name is written in peanut butter, like the PB in the logo: fat, puffy letters that glow a little in the middle.

It rests on top of the toast, half on and half off, and drips down onto it: 3 to 5 round drips, all different lengths.

Jelly from the chapter above lands on a letter, makes a little pile, and sometimes drips once. The letters always stay easy to read.

Short names only, so a title always fits on one line.

The buttons
Chapter 15 of 18

Puffy, drippy, and squishy.

Every button is a puffy marshmallow with 0 to 4 short running jelly drips, different every time it shows up. Grape Jelly is the jelly, Peanut butter is the PB. Delete gets a bite.

Small round buttons

BackShareDelete

Same colors as the big ones, Apple's icons in white, no drips. Stacked buttons sit 8 pt apart, and a long drip can land on the button below.

Panels you swipe down

Make a PBgif

Every panel you can swipe down wears a glob of peanut butter on its top edge, with a shiny down arrow in it. It sits up 9 pt above the edge and drips over it. Swipe down or tap outside to close.

Tap a button. It squishes. The drips only change when the page loads again. If someone has Reduce Motion turned on in iPhone settings, it just darkens.

The rules
Part 4 · The rules
Chapter 17 of 18

The house rules.

Nine of them. Tap one to open it.

1Burnt Toast for reading, Grape Jelly for tapping

In the app, titles and text are Burnt Toast and Grape Jelly marks only things you can tap. The tour and guide may also use Grape Jelly for headlines and labels.

2The slice wears its toasted rim

Always, on every use of the slice.

3Give it room

A quarter of the slice width on every side. The app icon is exempt.

4Never too small

Never smaller than: slice 48 pt, letters 32, flat 24, typed word 20 (a fingertip is about 44 pt). The badge on free PBgifs is the one exception.

5Letters must stand out

At least 3 to 1 against what's behind them. Plain brown letters on Lavender don't make it (2.2 to 1). With the dark PB edge they do (3.3 to 1), like the PB titles. Otherwise use the slice.

6Cloth, not behind words

The gingham cloth is a welcome background. Just never right behind reading text or a PBgif: those sit on a toast, card or plate.

7Brand colors on the brand

Buttons, words and screens use the brand colors. Anything goes inside the content (photos, PBgifs, seasonal recipes, ads), as long as the words are easy to read.

8Errors pop up, good news slides down

Every error is a pop-up with one fix button. Saved is a Burnt Toast bar.

9No dark mode

The app looks the same when the phone is set to dark.
